cases.title: Dwarka: audit design justification, then compare comparable costs
cases.summary: CAG questioned why an eight-lane elevated carriageway was chosen where 90 m right-of-way was available and questioned independent appraisal of ₹7,287.29 crore sanctioned civil cost. The frequently cited ₹18.20 versus ₹250.77 crore/km compares different design scopes.
cases.attribution: CAG Report 19/2023, paras 3.5.2.2 and 5.1.3–5.1.4; audit 2017–21 with 2023 updates.
cases.response: MoRTH’s April 2022 reply says grade separation and minimal access allow interstate traffic, existing local roads serve commuters, and underpasses were coordinated with authorities. The August 2023 reported reply disputes comparability and cites competitive bids. CAG rejoined that an at-grade carriageway with selected underpasses was a feasible alternative.
alternativeExplanations: Elevated structures, interchanges, utility coordination and urban constraints change unit cost.
Cabinet programme norm, sanctioned civil cost, award cost and total capital cost are different measures.
cases.falsifier: Obtain contemporaneous alternatives analysis, approved DPR, package BOQs and independent appraisal; a justified like-for-like engineering comparison could resolve or weaken the audit objection.

cases.title: Jagatpur–Dharampota: damage soon after renovation
cases.summary: CAG para 4.9 says road strengthening completed in March 2021 for ₹48.64 crore was damaged within seven months; ₹7.17 crore expenditure on affected stretches was unfruitful. A ₹12.85 crore permanent restoration estimate prepared in November 2021 remained unapproved in May 2025. This is an estimate, not proof that a second contract was paid.
cases.attribution: CAG West Bengal Report 1/2026, para 4.9, printed pp. 87–91 and Appendix 4.5.
cases.response: The department’s December 2023 / September 2024 reply cited vegetation, soil chemistry, steep slopes and unprecedented October 2021 flood velocity; it claimed 917 m damaged and 1,145 m repaired by the agency. CAG said known hydrology and soil needed design mitigation and cited a defect-liability relaxation request covering wider stretches.
alternativeExplanations: Extreme flood loading and expansive soil can require changed engineering design.
Contractor defect rectification, restoration estimate and new public payment must be resolved separately.
cases.falsifier: Match chainage-level damage, measurement books, defect-liability records, final repair certificate and any restoration award/payment; completed contractor-funded repairs would change the unresolved repeat-spending question.

cases.title: Bridge utilities: separate samples show coordination gaps
cases.summary: CAG examined 15 of 67 new bridges in 17 test-checked divisions: essential utility provisions beyond optical fibre and electric lamp posts were missing. In a separate 30-bridge joint-visit sample, five old bridges had unauthorised utilities. Separate verification found PHED pipelines on 14 bridges without prior PWD approval.
cases.attribution: CAG West Bengal Report 1/2026, paras 4.6.1–4.6.2.1; audited 2019–24, field visits in 2024.
cases.response: The department accepted the pipeline observation in April 2025 and said future bridge construction would consult stakeholders. Mansai bridge’s 2022 high-voltage cable was approved after bridge completion but had no designated duct.
alternativeExplanations: Utility demand can evolve after initial bridge construction; structural capacity must be checked before inferring actual damage.
These overlapping samples must not be summed into a single affected-bridge count.
cases.falsifier: Retrieve bridge-specific load assessments, approved utility drawings and remedial completion records; authorised capacity-checked installations would narrow the safety concern.

cases.title: Cherkkala slope collapse: reconstruction at concessionaire cost
cases.summary: After the 16 June 2025 NH66 slope-protection collapse, NHAI attributed failure to design, protection and drainage and announced debarment plus a show-cause notice for one year / up to ₹9 crore. The official release says the HAM contract requires 15-year maintenance and reconstruction at the concessionaire’s own cost.
cases.attribution: MoRTH/NHAI official statement of 17 June 2025; causes attributed to NHAI, not independently verified here.
cases.response: NHAI constituted a CRRI / IIT Palakkad / GSI expert committee. Contractor response and the final committee or debarment order were not located; no silence-as-admission inference is made.
alternativeExplanations: The same corridor’s 2022 VUP scaffolding incident is a different asset and failure mechanism.
Own-cost contractual rectification can explain two recorded works without two public payments.
cases.falsifier: Obtain the final expert report, contractor representation, final order and repair payment records; these could revise attribution, duration, penalty and who bore the cost.

cases.title: Meachi bridge: foundation settlement and river-flow constriction
cases.summary: NHAI reported about 600 mm settlement at pier P3, chainage 24+461 on Galgalia–Bahadurganj NH327E on 23 June 2023. The 222 m bridge was under construction and not open; the official release reported no casualties.
cases.attribution: MoRTH/NHAI release of 25 June 2023: preliminary investigation, not a final inquiry verdict.
cases.response: NHAI reported preliminary flow constriction and scour following increased river flow, ordered rectification and constituted an expert committee. Certain concessionaire and Independent Engineer personnel were suspended during inquiry; contractor response and final report were not retrieved.
alternativeExplanations: Sudden river flow, construction staging, scour protection and foundation design need joint assessment.
Temporary personnel suspension does not establish criminal or corporate culpability.
cases.falsifier: The final geotechnical/hydrological report, as-built drawings, method statement and contractor response could confirm or revise the preliminary cause and responsibility.

cases.title: UP electricity: overlapping manpower and project-management scopes
cases.summary: CAG paragraph 3.3.4 concluded that ₹46.27 crore paid to four manpower firms was infructuous because their scope substantially overlapped project-management agencies. Agreements were worth ₹73.47 crore; award value and paid amount are separate.
cases.attribution: CAG attributed audit finding
cases.response: Government (December 2023) said PMAs ensured implementation/quality while mission managers motivated households, organised camps and ledgerised e-sanyojan. Contracts were terminated when no longer required. Management (January 2024) said costs came from the PMA head. CAG rejected the distinction because PMA scope already covered concept-to-commissioning support.
alternativeExplanations: Surge capacity and household mobilisation can be legitimate separate outputs even where job descriptions overlap.
A repeated scope is not proof that the same worker-hour or asset was paid twice.
Actual deliverables, attendance, approval authority and termination accounts are needed; no post-audit recovery status established.
cases.falsifier: Reconcile company-level deliverables and invoices to show distinct contracted outputs, or produce audited recovery/settlement records that update the historical amount.

amounts.stage: paid amount characterised by CAG as infructuous

cases.title: UP electricity: duplicate connection payments and recovery trail
cases.summary: CAG reports ₹26.65 crore excess payments for duplicate connections across sampled grid and standalone-solar records (paragraphs 3.3.8–3.3.9). Matching keys varied across account numbers, meter numbers and names/addresses. The separately stated ₹4.41 crore solar category must not be added again to the headline.
cases.attribution: CAG attributed audit finding
cases.response: UPPCL directed verification and recovery in January 2024. In February 2024 management reported MVVNL would recover ₹6.53 crore; PuVVNL imposed ₹8.66 crore penalty and had recovered ₹4.54 crore; PVVNL recovery was made/in progress. DVVNL disputed some matches and described other recoveries. CAG acknowledged recovery action but rejected the claim that no DVVNL connections predated the scheme, citing 1,316.
alternativeExplanations: Same-name matches require household/connection identity verification.
Re-metering, replacement and migration can generate legitimate multiple records; scheme eligibility and actual bills distinguish them.
₹4.54 crore is a reported recovered amount for PuVVNL, not proof that the full ₹26.65 crore is recovered or still outstanding.

The report places the ₹26.65 crore headline inside 3.3.8; its five listed categories total ₹22.2351 crore, which with the ₹4.41 crore category in 3.3.9 rounds to ₹26.65 crore. Keep this aggregation note rather than double count.
cases.falsifier: Obtain the matched connection ledger, original installation/commissioning records and recovery receipts, reconcile duplicate categories without overlap, and update each DISCOM’s outstanding amount.

cases.title: Karnataka water: late tenders and the re-tender explanation

cases.response: Government (May 2025) cited timely administrative approvals, lack of bidder participation and repeated tender calls. CAG replied that only 13 of 33 tenders were recalled, so the explanation did not cover all tenders and central-share eligibility remained unanswered.
alternativeExplanations: Re-tendering can reflect insufficient competition, revised scope, or failed bids.
Tender value, award value, payment, completed asset and operational supply are different stages.
Later extensions or authorized revisions could change eligibility; none is inferred.
cases.falsifier: Retrieve all 33 tender IDs, corrigenda, bidder responses, cancellation/re-invitation links, award orders, authorized deadline extensions and central-share release decisions.

cases.title: Azamgarh schools: quality checks, incomplete works and revised costs
cases.summary: CAG paragraph 2.2 describes two KGBV buildings in Lalganj and Thekma remaining incomplete in June 2022 after starts in 2011, with ₹1.17 crore characterised as unfruitful spending. A ₹1.46 crore revised completion estimate and an earlier ₹2.01 crore reconstruction estimate must not be summed as payments.
cases.attribution: CAG attributed audit finding
cases.response: Government (June 2022) accepted that later instalments were released without quality reports; said substandard work was found in August 2015, responsible employees were terminated and an FIR lodged, and 50% of revised estimates was released in January 2022 with district transfer in progress. CAG said recovery/action against UPRNN and safeguards over re-allotment remained inadequate.
alternativeExplanations: The 2019 structural committee recommended repair/restoration instead of the earlier demolition/reconstruction proposal; changed remedial engineering explains different estimates.
School classes continued in transit premises; an incomplete building does not establish a closed school.
An FIR is not a conviction; individual employee identities and case disposition are not asserted.
cases.falsifier: Obtain revised technical sanction, quality reports, completion certificate, school occupancy record and recovery ledger; separately reconcile release-to-district, transfer-to-agency and certified work.

cases.title: Private schools: sanction-to-reimbursement differences need dated claims
cases.summary: Karnataka’s parliamentary table records FY2025-26 ₹156.10 crore sanctioned and ₹148.68 crore reimbursed to schools. The ₹7.42 crore arithmetic difference does not establish overdue debt, diversion or a tender irregularity.
cases.attribution: Analytic follow-up to a dated Ministry of Education parliamentary answer
cases.response: The Ministry’s 27 July 2026 answer says reimbursement is timely as informed by Karnataka. It describes the state’s 2018 neighbourhood-school exemption and a PRABANDH claim population covering elementary classes.
alternativeExplanations: Claims may be conditional, adjusted or not yet due; a sanction is not an unconditional payment obligation.
Private-school RTE reimbursement is distinct from capital works grants and foreign equity in a services company.
The state table including Bengaluru is not city-level spending.
cases.falsifier: Reconcile eligible school IDs, claim periods, state per-child rate, approved amounts, due dates and bank credits; overdue eligible claims rather than the aggregate difference would justify a payment-delay finding.

cases.title: Karnataka water: single-bid awards and missing contractor joins
cases.summary: CAG records 9,342 of 38,231 finalised in-village works awarded after single-bid participation on the first call (about 24%). Among those 9,342, 791 had tender premium above 5%, up to 61%. These are audited tender counts, not the share of villages with failed water supply or a finding that all awards were unlawful.
cases.attribution: CAG Karnataka JJM report, sections 3.7.1–3.7.2
cases.response: Government (May 2025) said mission-mode deadlines required expediting work under Finance Department directions. CAG said recall was the first option and negotiation was allowed in exceptional cases above 5% premium; mission mode could not be a blanket exception for all 791. On missing B15/e-procurement project and contractor links, Government said a Contract Management Module had been mandated in March 2025.
alternativeExplanations: Thin local supplier markets, geography, packaging and deadlines can produce a single bid without collusion.
A premium relative to an estimate does not alone prove overpricing; estimate vintage, scope and market inputs matter.
Anonymous bidder login IDs in Table 3.7 are not resolved legal-company or political identities; no names were guessed.
CAG audit population and the separate CPPP dataset are different universes and must not be pooled.
cases.falsifier: Retrieve tender-level bid logs, estimate versions, competent-authority exceptions, negotiation results, cancellation/re-invitation chains and the new module crosswalk; compare like-for-like works and authorized exceptions before attributing misconduct.

cases.title: Police vehicle financing: borrowing and budget repayment diverged
cases.summary: CAG records a ₹500 crore vehicle loan permitted in January 2018 through TSPHCL. Although the agreement required repayment from project revenue rather than budget allocation,₹328 crore paid by March 2022 came from budget resources. CAG estimated ₹13 crore extra interest against the State's average borrowing rate.
cases.attribution: CAG Telangana State Finances Report 2 of 2023, Box 2.4; audit calculation, not an independently adjudicated corruption finding.
cases.response: TSPHCL confirmed in November 2022 that it had borrowed on the Government's behalf. The report recommends full disclosure and a time-bound reform path for off-budget borrowing; a later repayment reconciliation was not retrieved.
alternativeExplanations: Administrative financing through a state corporation can fund legitimate assets; the concern here is the documented repayment/disclosure treatment, not the existence of police vehicles.
The ₹13 crore is an estimated borrowing-cost difference, not the whole loan being lost or diverted.
cases.falsifier: A corrected tripartite agreement, authenticated repayment ledger or subsequent CAG/PAC settlement showing an authorised different repayment basis would narrow or resolve the control finding.

cases.title: Safe City: supplementary provision and payment timing need reconciliation
cases.summary: For FY 2021-22 Hyderabad Safe City, CAG records ₹1 crore original provision plus ₹176 crore supplementary provision for pending bills, but only ₹12 crore expenditure. The denominator is ₹177 crore total provision; the ₹176 crore was the supplement, not the original budget.

cases.response: Commissioner of Police, Hyderabad said in November 2022 that savings were revalidated and released in 2022-23. CAG noted that the 2022-23 original provision was only ₹3 crore and questioned whether pending bills had been provided for.
alternativeExplanations: Multi-year works, revalidation and delayed billing can create timing differences; underspending alone does not establish theft or contractor favouritism.
Only the two referenced fiscal-stage records are assessed; later grants and actual payments could resolve the discrepancy.
cases.falsifier: Revalidation orders, FY 2022-23 supplementary grants and bill/payment ledgers that reconcile the pending liabilities would resolve the dated question.

cases.title: Warehouse construction delay prolonged rental spending
cases.summary: CAG reported 441 weeks between initiating the Chennai Canteen Stores Department warehouse proposal and sanction, versus a 48 week norm;₹17.43 crore rent was paid from October 2018 to December 2022. The contract was concluded in December 2022 with planned completion in November 2024.
cases.attribution: CAG Army Report 11 of 2024 official release, item 5.
cases.response: The summary attributes delay to processing by CSD/MES, sanction and later fund release by the Ministry. It does not reproduce a separate Ministry reply. November 2024 is a scheduled completion date, not verified completion.
alternativeExplanations: Hiring interim space can maintain services while construction is delayed; all rent is not automatically avoidable.
Sanction delays, funding and contracting delays are distinct stages and should not be charged twice as separate losses.

cases.title: Procurement preference did not authorise a higher payable rate
cases.summary: In one tested Bargarh boundary-wall tender, CAG found an award at ₹3.32 lakh where the applicable process should have awarded at ₹3.04 lakh, creating ₹0.28 lakh extra obligation. The flaw was applying the price-preference process incorrectly, not the existence of lawful preference.
cases.attribution: CAG Odisha e-Procurement Report 1 of 2025, para 2.7.2, printedp 16; one tested case among five bids.
cases.response: Department replied in December 2023 that privileged-bidder configuration was available. CAG considered that insufficient because the required business rules were not fully mapped into financial evaluation.
alternativeExplanations: A permitted social preference or lottery must be evaluated under its precise rules; a higher quoted bid is not automatically an irregular selection.
One audit sample cannot be extrapolated as a corruption rate for all government tenders or a bidder community.
cases.falsifier: Original tender terms, preference order, sanctioned comparison sheet and final paid bill demonstrating a different lawful payable rate, or an accepted audit settlement, could resolve the extra-obligation finding.

cases.title: Recruitment outsourcing and records: process cancellation with individual distinctions
cases.summary: On 3 April 2025 the Supreme Court upheld cancellation of West Bengal's 2016 school selection process with modified relief. It discussed OMR scanning/evaluation outsourcing and destroyed/missing records. It explicitly distinguished candidates specifically found tainted from those not specifically found tainted.
cases.attribution: Supreme Court 2025 INSC 437, especially paras 20–27 and 45–52; documented civil judgment.
cases.response: The State, Commission and appointees challenged the blanket remedy and raised segregation/evidentiary arguments. The Court maintained process cancellation but stated that not-specifically-tainted employees need not refund payments and may compete with age relaxation. Para 50 expressly preserves independent criminal proceedings.
